prophase.name: Stage 1: Prophase
prophase.description: First phase of mitosis: replicated chromatin condenses into distinct double-chromatid chromosomes, centrioles migrate to poles, and the nuclear envelope disintegrates.

metaphase.name: Stage 2: Metaphase
metaphase.description: Second phase of mitosis: chromosomes line up in single file along the equatorial metaphase plate, with spindle fibers attached to kinetochores.

spindle_fibers.name: Spindle Fibers (Microtubules)
spindle_fibers.description: Protein microtubule filaments that polymerize from centrosomes and attach to centromeres to mechanically maneuver and segregate chromosomes.

anaphase.name: Stage 3: Anaphase
anaphase.description: Third phase of mitosis: centromeres split and contracting spindle fibers pull sister chromatids apart to opposite poles as V-shaped daughter chromosomes.

centromere.name: Centromere (Kinetochore)
centromere.description: Constricted chromosome region that binds sister chromatids together and serves as the attachment point for kinetochore spindle fibers.

cleavage_furrow.name: Cleavage Furrow (Cytokinesis)
cleavage_furrow.description: Contractile ring of actin and myosin microfilaments that constricts the plasma membrane inward during animal cell cytokinesis.

telophase_cytokinesis.name: Stage 4: Telophase & Cytokinesis
telophase_cytokinesis.description: Final phase: daughter chromosomes reach opposite poles, nuclear envelopes reform, and a cleavage furrow pinches the cytoplasm into two genetically identical daughter cells.
